key_insight: The paper argues that the next bottleneck in autonomous scientific discovery is not better agent workflows, but better agent environments. By carefully engineering the resources, constraints, and interfaces that agents operate within, LLM agents can more effectively propose, test, and improve scientific solutions.
problem_solved: Current LLM agent systems for science often rely on hand-designed workflows, but these become less important as models improve. This paper addresses how to set up the environment so agents can autonomously discover solutions more reliably and efficiently.
method: Design the agent environment around the task's optimizable metric, so the agent can iteratively improve toward a measurable goal.
Provide the right execution resources, constraints, and interaction interfaces to guide exploration without manually scripting every step.
Enable a propose-validate-iterate loop in which the agent tests ideas, learns from results, and refines its own scientific solutions.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shifts attention from prompt chains and workflow engineering to environment design as a core lever for performance. It suggests a more scalable path to autonomous research systems that can outperform human-designed approaches in scientific discovery tasks.

paper_title: EurekAgent: Agent Environment Engineering is All You Need For Autonomous Scientific Discovery
paper_authors: Amy Xin, Jiening Siow, Junjie Wang, Zijun Yao, Fanjin Zhang
